leader.h1: Renovations in Cape Town, built for the Cape climate
leader.cta_line: Waterproofing, painting, kitchens and bathrooms. One team, one written quote, and a site that gets cleaned up at the end of the day.

home.intro_heading: What we do, and how we work
home.intro_body:
Most renovation work in Cape Town fails in the same three places: a wall that takes weather it was never detailed for, a wet area that was tiled before it was waterproofed, and a plan that changed halfway through without anyone writing down what it cost.

We work the other way around. We look at the building first, including the parts you cannot see once the work is finished. Roof falls, parapets, flashings, the base of a wall, the substrate under a screed. Then we write the scope down, price it, and build to it. If something changes on site, it goes into writing before it goes into the wall.

Our base is in Goodwood, which puts most of the Cape Town metro inside half an hour. We work on houses across the Northern Suburbs and Southern Suburbs, on bathrooms and kitchens, on full renovations and extensions, and on the waterproofing and damp work that those jobs usually turn up.
home.about_heading: A young company with something to prove
home.about_body:
We are a small Cape Town team, not a national franchise with a call centre. The person who quotes your job is on site while it runs, and the people doing the work are the people you met at the start.

We take on fewer jobs at a time so that each one gets a proper sequence: strip, repair, waterproof, tile, finish. We do not start a bathroom and disappear for two weeks. And we do not promise timelines we cannot hold, because the honest answer to how long a renovation takes depends on what is behind the tiles.

What we can promise is a written scope, a written price, and a call the same day if something changes. Ask us the awkward questions before you appoint anyone. We would rather answer them then than argue about them later.
home.services_intro: Six things we do properly, from the waterproofing that keeps a Cape house dry to the kitchens and bathrooms that make it worth living in.
home.areas_body:
We cover Cape Town from Goodwood outward: Durbanville and Bellville to the north, Parow and Brackenfell, the Table View and Milnerton coast, and the Southern Suburbs from Rondebosch down to Tokai. If you are further out, ask. Stellenbosch and Somerset West are worth the drive on a larger job.

The housing stock changes street by street. Older Parow and Bellville homes are solid masonry with plaster that has taken sixty years of weather, and they need different repair work to a 1990s Brackenfell house or a new build in Durbanville. That is why we look at the building before we quote the job.

whyus.point: One team from quote to handover
whyus.detail: The person who measures your job is accountable for the finish. No handover shuffle between a salesperson and a crew you have never met.
You get the stages, the materials and the exclusions in writing before work starts, so a variation is a conversation rather than a surprise invoice.
In Cape Town, waterproofing and paint prep decide whether a renovation lasts. We build for winter rain and south-easter wind, not for a photograph.
Dust sheets, daily sweep, rubble removed as we go. You are living in the house, and the site should not take over more of it than the job needs.

faq.q: How much does a renovation cost in Cape Town?
faq.a: It depends on scope, but the big drivers are whether services move, whether walls come down, and what finish level you choose. A bathroom refit and a full kitchen replacement sit in very different brackets. We measure, then quote in writing with the stages separated so you can see what each part costs.

faq.q: How long will my job take?
faq.a: A bathroom typically runs three to four weeks, a kitchen four to six, and a full renovation depends on how much structural and service work is involved. We give you a sequence with dates at the start, and we tell you the same day if something on site changes it.

faq.q: Do you take on small jobs?
faq.a: Yes, if it is the kind of work we do well. A damp wall, a leaking parapet, a single bathroom. We will tell you honestly if a job is too small for us to be worth your money.

We bring in registered specialists for defined work, such as electrical, plumbing and gas, because those need the right registration and certificates. The coordination, sequencing and finish stay with us.

faq.q: What is the difference between waterproofing and damp proofing?
faq.a: Waterproofing keeps water out from the outside: roofs, walls, balconies, wet areas. Damp proofing deals with moisture coming up through the base of a wall, usually rising damp, or water trapped inside the structure. They need different repairs, and treating one as the other is why so many damp walls get painted twice and stay wet.

faq.q: Can you work while we live in the house?
faq.a: For bathrooms, kitchens and interior work, yes, with dust screens and a clear daily routine. For a full renovation with structural work, we will tell you at quote stage whether staying is realistic, because some stages are not compatible with living there.

faq.q: Do I need plans or permits?
faq.a: Cosmetic work and like-for-like replacement usually do not. Extensions, new openings in structural walls, and changes that affect the building envelope normally do. We tell you at quote stage what needs approval before we start, rather than after.
We walk the job with you, list anything that needs correcting, and close it out. Final payment is against that walk, not against a promise that we will come back.

home.cta_subtext: Send us a few photos and a rough idea of what you want. We will tell you what is realistic before you spend anything.

services.name: Waterproofing
services.title_tag: Waterproofing Cape Town | Roofs, Balconies & Walls
services.meta_description: Waterproofing in Cape Town for flat roofs, parapets, balconies, box gutters and walls. We trace the entry point, repair the substrate, then membrane. Free estimate.

leader.h1: Waterproofing in Cape Town that survives the winter
leader.cta_line: We find where the water gets in, repair what is holding it, then apply the membrane. In that order.

services.intro_body:
Cape Town rain does not arrive politely. Between May and August it comes sideways on a north-west wind, hits a wall for six hours, and works its way into every failed joint, crack, coping and blocked outlet on the way down.

Most of the waterproofing we are called out to repair was applied over a surface that was never prepared, or over a detail that was already holding water. A membrane is a thin skin. If the screed under it is breaking up, or the water cannot get to an outlet, the skin will fail and the ceiling below will stain again next winter.

The first visit is a diagnosis. We look at where the water enters, not just where it shows up inside, because a stain in the hallway is almost never directly below the leak. We check roof falls and outlets, parapet copings, flashings, window and door heads, balcony edges, and the base of walls where damp shows as a tide line on the plaster.

If the plaster is blown or the substrate is wet, no membrane will hold until that is repaired and dried. We will tell you that plainly, even when it means the job is bigger than you hoped, because the alternative is doing it twice.
services.detail_heading: The details that decide whether it stays dry
services.detail_intro: Water gets in at the joints, not the middle of a wall. These are the four places we spend most of our time.

subitems.desc: Falls, outlets, scuppers and coping joints. If water ponds for more than a day after rain, the fall is wrong and the membrane is being asked to do a job drainage should be doing.

subitems.name: Balconies, stoeps and box gutters
subitems.desc: The edge detail, the upstand against the wall, and the outlet through the parapet. These are the three points where a balcony leaks into the room below it.

subitems.name: Wall base and rising damp
subitems.desc: A tide line at skirting height usually means moisture coming up through the masonry, not a leaking roof. That is a damp repair, and treating it as surface waterproofing wastes money.

subitems.name: Cracks, window heads and flashings
subitems.desc: Movement cracks wider than a hairline, failed sealant at frames, and flashings that were never dressed into the wall. Small details, and the most common source of winter call-outs.

services.name: Painting

services.intro_heading: Prep is the job. Paint is the last step.
services.intro_body:
A Cape Town exterior takes a beating that most paint systems were not specified for: salt air on the Atlantic side, wind-driven sand from the south-easter, hard summer sun on north and west walls, and then four months of rain.

Painting over a problem is the most expensive way to deal with it. Chalky old paint, salt bloom on new plaster, mould in a shaded corner, or a crack that keeps opening will all come straight back through a fresh coat. So the first part of the job is washing, scraping, filling and priming, and it is the part that takes the time.

Older masonry homes in Parow, Bellville and the Southern Suburbs often need a breathable system. Sealing a wall that needs to dry outward traps moisture inside the plaster, which is how you get bubbling paint and a damp smell eighteen months later. Newer plaster needs time and the right primer before it is sealed, especially where efflorescence keeps pushing salt to the surface.

Interior work is mostly about clean edges and a finish that survives real life: washable sheens in kitchens and passages, a flatter finish on ceilings, and proper protection for floors and furniture while we are in the house.

subitems.desc: Cracks raked and filled, stains sealed, edges cut in properly. Washable sheen in wet and high-traffic areas, flat where the light hits the ceiling.

subitems.name: Exterior walls and gables
subitems.desc: High-pressure wash, biocide treatment where mould has taken hold, crack repair, then a breathable exterior system suited to the wall's condition.

subitems.name: Trim, doors, windows and steel
subitems.desc: Sanding, priming bare timber, rust treatment and a suitable topcoat on steel. Coastal fixings and frames corrode fast and get the right system.

subitems.desc: Doors and drawer fronts removed, degreased, sanded and sprayed. A cheaper route to a new kitchen look where the carcasses are still sound.

services.intro_heading: The kitchen is a plumbing and electrical job wearing a cabinetry costume

Most kitchen budgets go wrong in the same place: the layout was never settled before the order was placed. Move the sink and you move the plumbing. Move the hob and you move the electrical and the extraction. Move a wall and you may be into structural work and approval.

We measure the room, check what the services will allow, and settle the layout with you before anything gets ordered or stripped. That sequence is what keeps a six week job from becoming a twelve week argument.

Then the build runs in order: strip out, first-fix plumbing and electrical, screed and tile, cabinetry install, counter templating, appliances, splashback, snag. Each stage depends on the one before it, which is why we do not let trades overlap just to look busy.

The other thing we are strict about is dust. A kitchen renovation happens inside a working house. We seal the doorway, extract where we cut, and clean at the end of each day rather than saving it for the last one.

leader.eyebrow: Showers, wet rooms and full refits

leader.cta_line: The tile is the visible part. The falls, screed and membrane underneath are what decide whether it lasts.

services.intro_heading: A bathroom is a wet room, not a tiled room
services.intro_body:
Every leaking bathroom we are asked to fix has the same fault somewhere: water was allowed to sit where it should have drained. A shower floor with no fall to the outlet, a membrane that stops at the tile line instead of turning up the wall, or a screed laid over a substrate that was never prepared.

So we treat the waterproofing as the job and the tiling as the finish. The floor gets a fall to the drain before anything else happens, the membrane turns up the wall behind the skirting line, and the shower gets the correct upstand at the entry. If the substrate is cracked or the old screed is breaking up, it comes out. Tiling over a failing base is the most common way to waste a bathroom budget.

After that it is a sequence: strip, first-fix plumbing and electrical, screed, membrane, flood test, tile, sanitaryware, sealant, snag. Three to four weeks for a typical refit, and we tell you at the start which parts of the house will be out of use and when.

Ventilation matters as much as the membrane. A bathroom that stays wet grows mould on the grout and paint, no matter how good the waterproofing is, so extraction and a door that can actually vent are part of the plan.

services.name: Damp Proofing
services.title_tag: Damp Proofing Cape Town | Rising Damp & Seepage
services.meta_description: Damp proofing in Cape Town. We diagnose rising damp, penetrating damp and condensation, then treat the cause and replaster with salt-resistant render.

leader.h1: Damp proofing in Cape Town, diagnosed before it is treated
leader.cta_line: Three different problems look identical on a wall. Treating the wrong one is why damp comes back.

services.intro_heading: Not all damp is rising damp
services.intro_body:
A tide line at skirting height usually means moisture is coming up through the masonry. But a patch high on a wall, mould in a corner, or paint bubbling around a window is a different fault with a different repair. Painting over any of them is a delay, not a fix.

The three we see most in Cape Town are rising damp, where ground moisture moves up through the wall because the damp course has failed or was never there; penetrating damp, where water comes through the wall from outside because of a defect, a bridged damp course or a raised external ground level; and condensation, where moist air meets a cold surface and the wall is not actually wet from outside at all.

We diagnose by looking at the building, not just the wall: external ground levels, paving against the wall, planters, downpipes, roof water, and the ventilation inside the room. Sometimes the fix is drainage and a gap between paving and plaster, not an injection course.

Where rising damp is genuine, the treatment is a damp course, either injected or installed, followed by replastering with a salt-resistant render. Ordinary plaster will pull salts back to the surface and the stain will return, whatever paint goes on top.
services.detail_heading: The four treatments, and when each applies
services.detail_intro: Diagnosis decides the treatment. These are the options, not a menu to pick from.

subitems.name: Rising damp
subitems.desc: Failed or missing damp course. Treated with an injected or physical damp course, then replastered with a salt-resistant system to stop the tide line returning.

subitems.name: Penetrating damp
subitems.desc: Water crossing the wall from outside. Fixed at the source: defective plaster, failed joints, bridged damp course, raised ground, leaking downpipes or roof water.

subitems.name: Condensation and mould
subitems.desc: Moisture from inside meeting a cold surface. Solved with ventilation, extraction, insulation and heating, not with a waterproof coating.

subitems.name: Salt-damaged plaster
subitems.desc: Blown, powdery plaster where salts have crystallised. Removed back to sound masonry, then replastered with a render designed to tolerate salts.

cost.note: We do not quote an injection course until we have established that the damp is rising. If the cause is external, the quote will be for external work, which is often cheaper than treating the wrong wall.

steps.detail: Moisture readings, external inspection, ground levels, drainage and ventilation. We write down what we found and what it means.
Damp course, external drainage, ground levels or ventilation, depending on what the diagnosis showed. No cosmetic work before this.
Salt-damaged plaster cut back to sound masonry so the new render has something to bond to and the salts are gone.
Salt-resistant render, appropriate finish, and a check after the first wet season to confirm the wall is behaving.

whyus.detail: Injection is not a cure-all. We identify which of the three damp types you have before quoting anything, and we will tell you when the answer is ventilation.
Ground levels, paving, downpipes and roof water get checked. A wall cannot dry out while it is standing in wet ground.
Correct render and finish after treatment, because ordinary plaster allows salts to migrate back and stain the new paint.
Where a wall will take a season to dry out, we say so at handover instead of letting you judge the job in week two.

services.cta_subtext: Send a photo of the wall with something in frame for scale, and tell us whether the damp is low, high, or in one corner. That usually narrows the cause before we arrive.
